results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records; and b. Audit-record time stamps meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and use Coordinated Universal Time, have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time, or include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: The two CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint (CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint) both carry ISO 8601 timestamps with the 'Z' (UTC) suffix (e.g., '2025-12-01T11:00:00Z' and '2026-03-15T14:22:00Z'). This demonstrates that: (a) AWS CloudTrail uses internal, NTP-synchronized system clocks to generate timestamps — satisfying AU-8.v4(a); and (b) timestamps are expressed in UTC with second-level granularity — partially satisfying AU-8.v4(b). However, the organization's formally defined granularity assignment (the '[Assignment: organization-defined granularity]' parameter in the control) was not available in the retrieved evidence. Without knowing whether the organization requires sub-second (e.g., millisecond) granularity, it cannot be confirmed that the second-level timestamps fully meet the defined threshold. Additionally, only CloudTrail events were available; any supplementary audit logging systems (e.g., application-level logs, SageMaker model monitor logs) were not assessed and may have different timestamp behaviors.
gaps: Organization's formally defined granularity requirement (e.g., seconds vs. milliseconds) for audit record timestamps is not documented in available evidence — human attestation or policy document review required.
No evidence retrieved for application-level or SageMaker-native audit logs; their timestamp format and UTC conformance could not be assessed.
No NTP/clock synchronization configuration evidence was available to independently verify the clock source used by the system.
